submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Fe 0.81, Sb 0.19) had the highest measured EQE, 0.055%. EQE rose steadily as Fe content went up: 0.005% at Fe 0.51, 0.032% at Fe 0.77 and 0.055% at Fe 0.81. This points to hematite-rich films as the active phase and puts the best composition at or near the Fe-rich end of the library.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE was 0.005%. MACE predicts FeSbO4 is stable and MEGNet predicts a gap below 2.7 eV, but it performed poorly anyway.
Measured EQE was 0.032%, lower than index 0.
Not measured. EQE fell as Sb content rose, and these compositions have no hematite.

consultations.verdict: Support: rutile FeSbO4 is on/near the hull (0.0016 eV/atom) and its predicted HSE gap (2.08 eV) is below the 2.7 eV photon energy, so it can absorb. Index 12 (Fe 0.51) sits at the FeSbO4 stoichiometry.

Weak support: the MEGNet HSE gap for hematite is 2.77 eV, which is borderline against 2.7 eV photons. Measured hematite has a gap of about 2.1 eV, so it should absorb. Index 12 (FeSbO4) gave a low EQE, so I'm testing the Fe-rich end (Sb-doped hematite plus some FeSbO4).

Mostly uninformative for index 2. The Sb-rich trirutile FeSb2O6 has a predicted gap of 1.28 eV, which says little about its PEC activity. The Sb-rich end has no hematite, and FeSbO4 already performed poorly, so I'm not measuring there. The measured data (EQE 0.055% at Fe 0.81 vs 0.005% at Fe 0.51) favor the Fe-rich region. I'm using the last measurement on index 2, near the current best, to probe the Sb-doping level in hematite.
